report.summary: PLAN-only review: the finite full-source evidence is sufficient in principle to publish source changes_suggested for a narrowly gated case, but the current gate at delivery-assessment.ts:472-482 is too wide and its evidence is weaker than the labelsIn witness contract claims. Three concrete gaps must be closed. (1) The candidate sent HTML set used for proof is the sourcePacket(sent) set, which excludes every non-HTML/CSS file; the coverage-completeness predicate at lines 144-149 only pins coverage.includedFiles against that set, so a delivery whose coverage either omitted or never listed an HTML file could still produce no_complete_group. (2) The descriptor labels mapped to unknown by the citation guard are never compared with the descriptor labels used by the full-source check: neither parse source nor labels identity is asserted, and no proof that the guard fired because of the label guard is kept. (3) The label witness itself returns an unlocated or foreign owner as unknown, which is correct, but it silently drops a form whose startOffset is unavailable, and per-node guard blocks can leave text with no location. Required minimal gating is: catalog_slots encoding; source_text (not manual-*/coverage-*) criterion; no linked business step; original raw status exactly supported; published status insufficient_evidence and a saved status-adjusted audit entry with originalStatus supported; nonempty, validated original citation IDs; the citation check returned incomplete with unknown across all cited files (never empty or unknown for a parse/owner/limit reason); the descriptor re-parsed as identical through the same parseSourceLiteralDirective path; coverage non-truncated, and every HTML-like path in the delivery inventory and in coverage.includedFiles is present in the proof set with the same bytes; the per-file labelsIn absence witness resolves with no unknown; then exactly no_complete_group, with per-page (PAGE) or per-resolved-form (FORM) semantics only, role aliases never mapped. Every other case (raw unknown, complete group present with missing cites, parse/foreign/implicit-owner/coverage uncertainty, empty cites, runtime or business-mapped) must stay insufficient_evidence on the existing path. The change would record the original supported status only in the existing status-adjusted audit and would not credit the model or alter citations, and it would not accept or pay. Critique: without these gates, the plan would let missing citations or a non-sent file masquerade as independent source absence, so the verdict is conditional sufficiency, not the current plan as written.

findings.title: Proof set for no_complete_group is the sent subset, but completeness check only pins coverage.includedFiles to it
findings.evidence: sourcePacket (lines 77-81) includes only html/css files; HTML paths in delivery.files that are not classified html are pushed to omittedFiles. createAssessmentLabelSourceFactsCheck is built from this `sent` map and its coverage (line 273). Inside lib/assessment-label-citations.ts lines 144-148, `html` is derived from the proof map itself, and the completeness predicate compares `observedCoverage.includedFiles` with `snapshot` keys. A coverage record that omits an HTML file from BOTH includedFiles and omittedFiles, or a delivery whose coverage was filtered before reaching the check, satisfies this predicate. The result is no_complete_group (line 165) even though an HTML file was delivered but never scanned.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): delivery.files has index.html and about.html; coverage.includedFiles=['index.html'], omittedFiles=[], truncatedFiles=[]. The proof map has only index.html, so the predicate at line 147 (`html.some(file => !observedCoverage.includedFiles.includes(file))`) checks nothing. index.html has only 'Name'; labels are 'Name','E-mail'; therefore the function returns no_complete_group with files ['index.html']. The stored coverage did not account for about.html.
findings.suggestion: Before publishing, require that every HTML-typed path in the validated delivery inventory, and every HTML path present in coverage.includedFiles or omittedFiles, appear in the proof set. Also require that proof bytes equal delivery bytes for those paths. Otherwise return unknown: incomplete_source.

findings.title: Unknown is triggered whenever the citation guard returns any non-covered result; it is not evidence that the citation guard specifically lowered supported because of incomplete label citations
findings.evidence: Line 139 collapses all non-covered outcomes to `reason: citation_witness`. Inside the guard (lines 192-194 and 197), non-covered includes: non-html citation files only, the 40-file or 262144-unit overflow, unsafe offsets, an excerpt mismatch, a file ending not `.html`, and the global multiple-complete-groups unknown. createAssessmentLabelSourceFactsCheck re-parses the criterion source independently, but nothing compares the descriptor labels/context actually lowered with the `labels`/`context` it uses for proof, and nothing records that the guard actually ran over the same labels.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): the criterion source parses to labels ['Name','E-mail']. The model cited an excerpt that is not a substring of the cited file. The guard returned unknown. The fact check then runs a full-source scan and can return no_complete_group although the citation guard never assembled per-label coverage (it failed at the byte check at line 194). The qualification 'actual label citation guard lowered' is not verified, and the unknown reason is misattributed.
findings.suggestion: Make the guard expose an explicit, parse-source-keyed 'incomplete/unknown' result only after labels are assembled (citations nonempty and valid, at least one `.html` cited file, within limits), and pass that descriptor identity to the fact check. Require the fact check's parsed descriptor to be identical before continuing. Label anything else citation_witness.

findings.title: Label-guarantee adjustment is not restricted to catalog_slots source_text criteria, and the audit/citation preservation is only assumed, not enforced by the call site
findings.evidence: The branch runs for any catalog_slots item not in insufficient_evidence, including `supported` (line 138 path) and `changes_suggested`. It also runs for every criterion id, including manual-*/coverage-* and structural ids. The changes_suggested branch returns no_complete_group with no re-derivation that the criterion is source_text. In the audit, publishSourceAssessmentNotes builds adjustedCriteria from the map of original statuses (lines 108-112); that works for supported→insufficient_evidence, but the call site does not itself guarantee that the check's citations are the validated nonempty ones (empty cites are only filtered later at line 453 for non-insufficient).
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): a criterion with original raw supported and empty citations reaches line 423; labelCitationCheck returns incomplete with an empty missing list, the item becomes insufficient_evidence, then line 474 passes status='insufficient_evidence' to the fact check, which can return no_complete_group. The branch is also reachable from a criterion id outside source_text.
findings.suggestion: In the changes_suggested branch of the fact check, return not_applicable/unknown unless the cited check was incomplete from a nonempty, validated citation set. In the caller, gate line 474 on labelCoverage.kind === 'incomplete' recorded for that item and on the criterion's source_text scope, so empty-citation or unknown-guard items never reach the absence proof.

findings.title: An unlocated form is grouped under the literal string 'unlocated', which can merge distinct forms and falsely yield one complete group or falsely pair labels
findings.evidence: Line 50 uses `String(node.sourceCodeLocation?.startOffset ?? 'unlocated')` as the group key. Two forms without source locations (e.g. synthesized by a large parse where locations are unavailable) share the group key. In context 'form' their labels are unioned by lines 155-162, so a complete group may appear across two distinct forms. Conversely, a form paired with located controls leaves owner `!== label.form`.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (unexecuted): contact.html has two forms without source locations. Each has one of 'Name' and 'E-mail'. The fact check for FORM context finds the group 'unlocated' with both labels and returns source_disagrees_with_change (line 163), which is a fail-closed outcome. In the guard direction (createAssessmentLabelCitationCheck, line 198, labelsIn without absence) it can produce a false complete group; there the result is 'covered', not a fail-open.
findings.suggestion: Treat an unavailable form location as unresolved ownership: return unknown (unresolved_parse_or_owner) when any form is unlocated and the context is 'form'. Do not use a constant placeholder as an owner key.

limitations: No files, runtime, tests, browser, provider or shell were executed; all conclusions are static reasoning over the supplied packet.

The packet does not include source-literal-directive.ts, native-form-source.ts, source-presence-evidence.ts, assessment-evidence-needs.ts, contracts.ts or the evaluation runner. Therefore parsing exactness of parseSourceLiteralDirective, the behavior of helpers called at lines 152-166, and contract shape of statusAdjustedCount/withheldRisks were not verified.

The true sent-HTML inventory equals sourcePacket's html/css set only if staticFileKind classifies every deliverable HTML file as 'html'. That function was not supplied, so the P1 evidence shows a gate that is insufficient at the call site, not a confirmed reachable production bypass.
Only two known false-pass fixtures (cycle40-plan-context) were available; no live holdout or new model outputs were supplied, so coverage for other failure modes remains unverified.
Award/champion comparison required by AGENTS.md is out of scope for a PLAN-only source critique and was not performed.
